lane: L1b — adapter turn-submission surface for command handlers
spec: evidence/ulw/requirements/20260918T001246Z/contract.md §2.1-§2.2 (the t1 freeze): a command handler runs 'without sending the command to the model', so starting a run needs the agent turn seam `agent.followup(message)` (in-tree precedent packages/mpd-agent-teams-plugin/lib/command.js); §2.2 leaves the seam NAME to the implementer and requires its own capability flag; the pre-step gesture needs no new seam because onEvent forwards to ctx.on verbatim.

reported_names.handler_surface: invocation.submit(message) => boolean (bound by registerCommand on a COPY of the host invocation)

changed_files.change: DshCapabilities.turnSubmit; DshAdapter.submitUserTurn(agent, message) with measured JSDoc (installed dsh-agent-loop followup => send(input,'next-turn',true)); DshCommandInvocation.submit?; the turn-plane implementation (feature-detected on a callable agent.followup, bound call, never throws, boolean result); registerCommand now hands the plugin {...hostInvocation, submit} so the host's invocation object is never mutated and the plugin never reads agent.followup; capabilities() reports turnSubmit from a live-registry probe.

fakeHarness() sample agent gained the host turn seam (followup captures submissions); new 'turn plane' describe (3 tests): handler submits through its invocation without mutating the host object; submitUserTurn reaches the followup (identity of the message) with every absent/broken surface a safe no-op; capabilities().turnSubmit truthful for a present and an absent agent surface.
the 14-check host probe (installed harness by absolute path).

verify.key_output: 54 pass / 0 fail / 191 expect() calls (51 before t12; +3 turn-plane tests). Includes every t3 test.
9 pass / 0 fail (t3 regression guard, re-run after the t12 edit)

probe_checks.A1.installed-followup-delegates-next-tur: the installed dsh-agent-loop source contains exactly `followup(input) { this.send(input, "next-turn", true); }` — the semantics the seam promises
probe_checks.A2.method-lives-on-the-live-agent-class: the method sits in `ReactLoopAgent`, which that package does NOT export; a live Agent from the registry is the only reachable handle
probe_checks.B1/B2/B3: the seam returns true, calls followup with `this` === the agent handed in, and passes the message object verbatim
probe_checks.B4/B5: five absent/broken surfaces (no followup, undefined, null, a string, a throwing driver) all return false and never throw
probe_checks.C1/C2: capabilities().turnSubmit is true with a live agent exposing followup, false for an agent without it and for a composition with no agent registry
probe_checks.D1/D2/D3: a registered handler's `invocation.submit(message)` returns success, the host's own invocation object gains NO `submit` key and keeps its keys, and the submission reaches the agent
probe_checks.D4: the submitted message still matches the installed dsh-llm createUserMessage source tag and is frozen
probe_checks.D5: the adapter surface exposes submitUserTurn and NO steer/inject/send

honest_bounds: No live Agent: the installed `ReactLoopAgent` (which owns followup) is not exported and needs a scoped cordis context plus a full Session, so the probe measures the INSTALLED SOURCE of followup and the adapter-side binding contract. The live end-to-end path (a real agent from a real boot) is t2/t7's live case.

turnSubmit is a LIVE-REGISTRY probe (same shape as compactionForAgent): a composition with no live session reports false although the surface exists. The authoritative per-call gate is the boolean returned by submitUserTurn / invocation.submit.

t3's recorded file hashes (evidence/ulw/l1-adapter-command/20260918T001851Z/result.json) describe the t3 revision; t12 supersedes the two adapter files, and this sweep re-ran the whole adapter suite (54 pass) plus the codegraph regression (9 pass).
